answer_1.quote: We create and release a large benchmark for meta-evaluating summarization metrics including: • Outputs from 25 top-scoring extractive and abstractive summarization systems on the CNN/DailyMail dataset.
answer_1.outputs: System-generated extractive and abstractive summaries evaluated against reference summaries.

answer_2.quote: We examine eight metrics that measure the agreement between two texts, in our case, between the system summary and reference summary. BERTScore (BScore)... MoverScore (MScore)... JS divergence (JS-2)... ROUGE-1 and ROUGE-2... ROUGE-L...

answer_4.quote: Manual evaluations using the lightweight pyramids method, which we use as a gold-standard to evaluate summarization systems as well as automated metrics... Workers are paid... For each document, we identify a "noisy" worker... we obtain a total of 10,000 human annotations... we use the majority vote to mark the presence of an SCU in a system summary.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators mark each Semantic Content Unit (SCU) as "present" if it can be inferred from the system summary, otherwise "not present"; majority vote determines final SCU presence.
